title: The Mystery of the Mary Celeste
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Mary Celeste, the 1872 American brigantine found drifting empty in the Atlantic near the Azores with no one aboard. They trace the ship's unlucky history from its Nova Scotia launch as the Amazon, through its maiden-voyage captain's death and later groundings, to Captain Benjamin Briggs's fateful final voyage with his wife and daughter. They cover the salvage claim by the crew of the Dei Gratia, Gibraltar Queen's Proctor Frederick Solly-Flood's suspicious investigation, the later Haiti insurance-fraud wreck by Captain Gilman Perkins, Arthur Conan Doyle's fictional account, and the theories of what happened, favoring a fear of an alcohol explosion that led the crew to abandon ship in the lifeboat. A listener mail segment closes the episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and holiday chat
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck catch up after the holiday break, with tangents about orchids, miniature crime scenes, and tiny Tabasco bottles, before introducing the Mary Celeste mystery.

segments.title: The dinner at the Astor House and the two captains
segments.summary: Captains David Morehouse and Benjamin Briggs dine in New York in November 1872 before both set sail for the Mediterranean. A month later Morehouse's ship Dei Gratia finds the Mary Celeste with no one aboard.

segments.title: Early history of the Amazon and its unlucky voyages
segments.summary: The ship, launched in Nova Scotia as the Amazon, has a run of misfortune: its first captain dies after a maiden voyage is aborted, its second captain's ship collides with another vessel, and it runs aground in a storm and is abandoned. It is bought as a wreck and rebuilt by James Winchester, with Briggs becoming a major investor and captain.

segments.title: Pool renovation tangent and break
segments.summary: Brief banter about a pool renovation show and a mid-episode break.

segments.title: Briggs's family voyage and the final departure
segments.summary: Briggs brings his wife Sarah and two-year-old daughter Sophia Matilda on the voyage, leaving son Arthur behind, and selects a crew of upright men. The Mary Celeste sails from New York in November 1872 carrying about 1,701 barrels of denatured alcohol, bound for Genoa.

segments.title: Final days, the log slate, and the discovery
segments.summary: Briggs changes course after failing to sight the Azores on his chronometer reckoning. The log slate records sighting land near Santa Maria. The Dei Gratia crew later sights the Mary Celeste and sends Oliver Deveau and John Wright to board, finding no one aboard, with the sounding rod, a disassembled pump, and personal belongings still present.

segments.title: Salvage claim, Gibraltar court, and Solly-Flood's suspicions
segments.summary: Deveau and two others sail the Mary Celeste to Gibraltar and file a salvage claim. Queen's Proctor Frederick Solly-Flood suspects foul play, suppresses test results showing the sword stain was rust, and the court awards the salvors a fraction of the value.

segments.title: Gilman Perkins's Haiti wreck and insurance fraud
segments.summary: The ship is released and sent to Genoa under a new crew, then runs aground off Haiti under Captain Gilman Perkins in an insurance fraud scheme. The salvager finds the claimed valuable cargo replaced with junk, and Perkins is tried for barratry, narrowly escaping execution.

segments.title: Conan Doyle's fiction and popular legends
segments.summary: Arthur Conan Doyle's fictional J. Habakuk Jephson's Statement in Cornhill Magazine helped spread the legend with invented details such as hot tea and a burning cigar. Later embellishments and a 1930s film added more fiction.

segments.title: Theories of what happened
segments.summary: The hosts review theories including sea quakes, waterspouts, giant squid, mutiny, murder, piracy, and paranormal causes, and discuss physical clues. They favor the theory that the crew feared an explosion from the alcohol fumes and abandoned ship in the lifeboat, which was later lost at sea. A 2006 University College London test simulated such an explosion.

segments.title: Listener mail from Sally
segments.summary: A listener named Sally, a sophomore at Emory University, describes discovering the show while on exchange in Beijing and thanks the hosts.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank listeners and give social media, email, and website contact details.
